# reac-pw

reac-pw is a PipeWire-native endpoint for Roland's REAC audio-over-Ethernet protocol: a daemon that puts a REAC network into the PipeWire graph as audio nodes. [FreeREAC/reac-pw](https://github.com/FreeREAC/reac-pw) · OSS-Fuzz: no project for reac-pw

**Status: available.** Of reac-pw's own fuzz targets, which OSS-Fuzz does not run, statements cover 7 of 7. 28 binaries, 9.0 MB. 51 statements: 47 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 4 open.

Built from reac-pw 1.0.42 (commit `f86a30a3`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz_segconf](fuzz_segconf/) | Reads one to four operator configuration texts made from the input (drop-in files under fuzz-chosen labels, then the main file) with the configuration reader, then compares every segment, role, model, ignore switch, provenance, refusal and declared VLAN with what the harness predicts from its own reading of the documented grammar, checks that a `knock` line is refused with its reason, and probes names no section opened. | 10 checks (api-contract, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_pin](fuzz_pin/) | Takes flags and a text from the input and parses the text as a --box MODEL[:LABEL] pin, optionally with missing arguments, and compares the result, the model row and the label with what the pin grammar and the box-model table predict. | 3 checks (reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_headamp](fuzz_headamp/) | Builds a PipeWire Props object from the input, keeping a record of what it wrote, and parses its head-amp control keys into a cell array of a fuzz-chosen capacity, with and without a result record; checks the count, the cells, the keys counted, the first refusal and that nothing is written past the capacity. | 8 checks (differential, invariant, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_rate](fuzz_rate/) | Builds a PipeWire Props object from the input and parses its sample-rate key; then decides the parsed rate and a second input rate for a master or slave with a fuzz-chosen drivable mask, and writes the drivable-rate list into a fuzz-sized buffer, comparing each answer with the closed rate list and the record of the object written. The key and the refusal enumeration come from libreac's configuration header; the harness works out each rate's bit from its own closed list and names each refusal code itself. | 7 checks (api-contract, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_role](fuzz_role/) | Builds a PipeWire Props object from the input and parses its role key, then works out whether the requested role changes the running one, comparing the answers and the published refusal codes with the role grammar and the record of the object written. The key, the role values and the answers come from libreac's configuration header. | 5 checks (api-contract, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_qdisc](fuzz_qdisc/) | Computes up to seven catch-up budgets under the etf qdisc, each from a lead in microseconds and a frame rate (from a fixed list that includes zero, a negative rate and the largest int) taken from the input, and compares each with the harness's own arithmetic. The qdisc counter read this harness used to drive is now libreac's and is not part of this program. | 1 check (reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 9, 9 proved |
| [fuzz_link](fuzz_link/) | Runs a sequence of input-chosen operations against a fake kernel netlink socket: read an interface's alias and link kind, write an alias, mark and unmark served interfaces, and decide a verdict from a kind and alias; checks requests, return codes, buffer bounds, socket use and the kept marks against a model of the kernel and the marking policy. The harness points the marking code's messages at a fixed buffer in memory, so the run writes none of them; no check depends on them. | 9 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 3 proved |

## What the statements say, for reac-pw
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Known issues
None known.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch reac-pw
    ./oft verify-sha reac-pw

By hand: download `reac-pw-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.11.1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1), unpack it into `projects/reac-pw/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; a testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [FreeREAC/reac-pw](https://github.com/FreeREAC/reac-pw) at `f86a30a3d06e84e8a7d6ec647cae77c4cbc9137b` (1.0.42), built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. The OSS Verify port `projects/reac-pw` at `ba46d3675f547098bca08b6353af0f1f8d61549f` in `theorem-labs/oss-verify` built every binary of this project instead of a build recipe. Its archive [`reac-pw-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src) holds the port's `tools/check`, which builds them again on this image with Docker: it fetches the project's source trees over the network, at the commits and SHA-256s the port pins, and does not read `reac-pw-src.tar.zst` ([docs/reproducing.md](../../docs/reproducing.md)).

## Licence
reac-pw is under `GPL-3.0-or-later`. Each binary is a combined work of reac-pw, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.11.1-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src): `reac-pw-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `reac-pw-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and [`reac-pw-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src), the port archive at `ba46d3675f547098bca08b6353af0f1f8d61549f` holding its `infra/`, `tools/` and `projects/reac-pw/` files: the build scripts, and the source of the driver linked into these binaries. Its binaries are under a GPL-family licence, so their corresponding source also takes `toolchain-src.tar.zst`, the source of the toolchain they were built with, in release [sources-v1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/sources-v1).
